v1_problem: Billing dispute tickets doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-02). This is not explained by slow dispute handling (median 1.6d/p90 2.8d within the 3.0d SLA, E-03) nor a tariff change (none logged, E-04). A majority of disputed bills (1785 of 3025) are built from ACTUAL, not ESTIMATED, reads (E-01), indicating the billing import/validation step itself is producing wrong bills from accepted reads for most disputes, concurrent with a manual meter-read route-completion shortfall (0.88 vs 0.95 target, 9200 accounts, E-05) that is a secondary contributor via the remaining estimate-substituted disputes.
v2_problem: Billing dispute tickets doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-02), not explained by response-time SLA breach (E-03) or a tariff change (E-04). Of 3025 disputed bills, the 1240 ESTIMATED-read bills (matching E-01 exactly) sit entirely on AMI read_channel accounts: 1184 (95.5%) had a valid pre-cutoff AMI read that was exported but rejected at billing import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (E-12). This is explained by validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, which compares raw register values directly against 12-month m3 consumption history with unit_scaling='none' (E-13), while firmware v4.2 meters (rollout 2026-06) report registers in units of 0.1 m3 rather than m3 (E-14) — causing legitimate high-usage v4.2 reads to appear roughly 10x inflated and be wrongly rejected, forcing estimate substitution and incorrect bills for that cohort.
